Definition: Galal, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Galal is a Levite, named twice among the families who served in the temple. He stands in the list of Levites in 1 Chronicles 9:15, and in Nehemiah 11:17 his grandson Mattaniah leads the thanksgiving in prayer, as the son of Micha, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph — with Abda the son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun. His name survives because his family sang.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Levites who sang are the backbone of Israel's worship. Galal's name is kept because his sons led the thanksgiving, and I hold that a family that sings God's praise leaves a longer mark than a family that builds an empire.
